intro: Consecutive repeated values can be represented as segments. Run-length encoding preserves order, unlike a frequency table that merges equal values from distant positions.
task: Compress consecutive runs while preserving boundaries between equal values that occur in separate segments.
requirements: values is a finite numeric vector, possibly empty. Compare neighboring values using exact equality, not a tolerance.
Return dict values as one numeric representative per consecutive run, lengths as integer run lengths, and starts as integer starting indices.
The decoded sequence repeats each representative by its corresponding length. Equal values separated by a different value must remain separate runs.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find transition indices
hints.body: A new run begins at zero and wherever adjacent values differ.

hints.title: Use a final sentinel
hints.body: Appending the sequence length to run starts makes run lengths simple differences.

explanation: Run-length encoding exploits local repetition. The run lengths sum to the original sequence length, and the start positions recover each segment boundary.
Exact equality is part of the format. Approximate grouping would require a different, potentially lossy contract for floating-point observations.
